newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK RAISES MAIN LEV RATE TO 5.59 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK RAISES MAIN LEV RATE TO 5.59 PCT.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has raised its main lev interest rate to 5.59 percent annually from 5.50 percent, effective Monday, dealers said on Thursday.

A BNB official said the rate rise reflected rising yield on three-month discount T-bills auctioned on Monday. Yield to maturity on the paper was 1.40 percent, up from 1.38 percent at the previous regular auction a week earlier.
This was the second rise in the main rate in as many weeks from 5.42 percent two weeks ago.
Under a memorandum of economic policy agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in March, the BNB adjusts the main interest rate weekly to the yield on three-month government securities.
The main rate had been steadily falling since March when Bulgaria sealed a 14-month $510 million standby agreement with the IMF and financial stabilisation began taking hold.
The rate stood at 18 percent monthly in March following a lev slump to 3,000 to the dollar in February amid political and administrative instability.

Bulgaria introduced a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime known as a currency board from July 1 to restore confidence in the financial system and the lev. The lev was pegged at 1,000 to the mark as an anchor currency. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
